name: RQGM v3 (synthesis): a prose-first, fail-closed loop with an optional read-only audit (rqgm_check.py). Grafts: command-gated variants, full-panel pruning, merit-only stalls, a 5-call seeded probe, and staged S/B/V/P validation.
thesis: Most runs happen where no code runs, so every safety rule stays in SKILL.md and in the INITIATOR paste block. Each rule is local, fails closed, and can be recomputed from logged verdicts. v3 adds: verdict/UNKNOWN/ERROR results, command-gated variants, pruning that needs a full 3-judge panel, a 5-call seeded probe, stalls that count merit outcomes only, results that stand until *best* changes, and a labelled Output. The stdlib read-only rqgm_check.py audits the log and never decides. A rule is enforced by code only after its misapplication is measured. v3 stays 'design review' until a logged run on a task.

controller.rationale: In scope only as a read-only, optional auditor (skills/rqgm-loop/rqgm_check.py), never as the acceptance authority. All three judges picked prose-first and vetoed an owning controller: rqgmctl-style next/record, reservations, a hash chain, lock, fsync, segments, COMPLETION_UNKNOWN, per-call keys, a TTY-only human op, and a live C arm. The bookkeeping the prose cannot carry reliably is handled in three ways. (1) It is reduced to record-derived forms the prose can carry: round-atomic resume with log-before-write replaces per-call keys; rounds and time come from records, with tokens null unless the host reports them, replacing a usage ledger; the stall count is defined from outcomes. (2) It moves to a command: hashes come only from 'rqgm_check.py hash', never from a model. (3) It is recomputed afterwards: audit replays every keep, drop, Check, halt and exit from the verbatim un-blinded verdicts. This is the smallest thing that turns 'trust the orchestrator' into 'audit the orchestrator'. It also gives the pilot a zero-model-call conformance suite and the Stage-1 answer keys, and it keeps a code-free host first-class. It becomes enforcing only by pre-registered promotion: if Stage-1 misapplication reaches 3/30 or more in any context, or any rule class is wrong in 2 of 3 contexts, or a pilot P run shows a decision-changing VIOLATION or a journal mismatch, that rule becomes checker-mandatory where a shell exists (v3.1) and a live enforcing arm is scheduled.

cli_ops.name: audit MEMORY [--done DONE.json] [--target DIR] [--pending ROUND.json] [--first]
cli_ops.behavior: Read-only: no network, no model, no clock (times come from record fields). Parses archive.jsonl. An unparsable or newline-less last line is torn_tail: it is excluded and reported. An interior unparsable line is INTEGRITY: exit 2, and nothing after it is audited. It rebuilds state: best id, rung, probe mode per rung, stall count s, error streak e, rounds and minutes used, tokens or null, the standing Check per (version, rung, amend-epoch), open required gaps, held-out attempts, amends, the step due next (round|check|boundary|heldout|halt:REASON|exit), and the recomputed status ACTIVE|PARTIAL|COMPLETE. It recomputes every logged decision by decision_policy and prints JSON {ok, state, violations:[{code, class: VIOLATION|RECORD|AMBIGUOUS, record_index, expected, actual}], unauditable:[{rule, missing_field}], warnings, torn_tail}. Exit 0 = no VIOLATION, 1 = violations, 2 = integrity or usage error. A missing field makes that rule unauditable, never violated, so v2-format archives degrade gracefully. --first stops at the first VIOLATION and evaluates no later decision (shadow-replay semantics; it never splices later outputs). --pending audits a not-yet-logged round as if appended and prints {required_keep, outcomes, next_due}; this is the Stage-1 answer key and an optional in-loop pre-check. --done compares DONE (after applying logged amends) with setup.done. --target hashes setup.check_files against setup.check_hashes. Never writes any file.

cli_ops.name: selftest
cli_ops.behavior: Runs tests/checker/fixtures/*.jsonl against expected.json. Each negative fixture must yield exactly its codes and classes, with no extras. Each positive conformance fixture must yield none. The --first fixture must yield only its first violation. The v2-format fixture must return ok=true with its rules listed as unauditable. No network, model or clock. Exit 0 only if all match, so a checker that rejects everything fails.

cli_ops.name: hash FILE... [--lf]
cli_ops.behavior: Prints the SHA-256 of each file (--lf normalizes CRLF to LF first). This is the only source of hashes in MEMORY (setup.check_hashes); the prose never requires a hash.

controller.decision_policy: The checker recomputes; it never decides. (0) VALUES: judge values are un-blinded to variant|best|tie|UNKNOWN|ERROR. 'Completed' means variant|best|tie. Slot 1's two orders map to one value if they are equal, else UNKNOWN; this applies overall and per criterion, and the logged overall must equal it. (1) BASELINE AND PROTECTED: v0's commands and sources come from check{trigger:setup}. Protected(round) = must-not-change ids ∪ ids with guardrail:true ∪ ids whose latest value on round.best is pass (the kept variant's gate commands or the last Check). (2) GATES, in order: a variant that fails any gate has no verdicts. Apply must be 'ok'; an ERROR may be retried once, then the outcome is dropped. Every command criterion needs pass|fail; an ERROR after one retry means dropped. A 'fail' on a protected command criterion means rejected (REGRESSION). A 'fail' where best also fails is allowed. screen 'reject:*' means rejected. (3) PANEL, normal mode: slot 1 is required. Early drop (outcome rejected, no slot 2) if slot 1 is best with confidence high, or has any protected criterion = best. Otherwise slot 2 is required. Slot 3 is required unless slots 1 and 2 are both variant or both best (tie and UNKNOWN never skip slot 3). Strict mode (the probe for the current rung has mode strict): slots 1-3 are required and there is no early drop. A slot may be retried at most once; a second ERROR means dropped. A missing required slot on a non-dropped variant is JUDGE_MISSING. (4) ELIGIBILITY: IMPROVE if #variant ≥ 2 (strict: 3), #best = 0, and no completed slot has a protected criterion = best. PRUNE if words < best.words, all 3 slots are completed, every overall is variant or tie, and no per-criterion value in any slot is best or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN and ERROR never add to any count; they only block PRUNE. Confidence matters only for the early drop. (5) SELECTION: among eligible variants, take max #variant, then fewer words, then list order. Exactly that one has outcome kept and is round.kept; if none is eligible, kept is null. version.parent = round.best = the previous kept id (or v0). version.diff equals the kept variant's judged diff. (6) STALL: s counts rounds since the last keep or rung change where kept is null and at least one variant was not dropped. e counts consecutive rounds where every variant was dropped; e = 2 requires exit{PARTIAL, ERROR} next. A Check is due at s = 3 or on check{trigger:claim}. A round logged while a Check is due and missing is MISSED_CHECK. (7) CHECK: at most one per (version, rung, amend-epoch); a later one is RECHECK_UNCHANGED and the first one stands. Command and source values are as logged; a source pass needs a verified citation for that criterion when citations carry criterion ids, otherwise it is unauditable. A judges criterion passes if #pass ≥ 2 of 3 votes (strict: 3); UNKNOWN and ERROR are not pass. A mismatch with the logged value is CHECK_MISCOUNT. Held-out failing ids on version v count as failing in v's standing result. After a Check: all required pass → the next record must be the boundary (below the final rung: rung{} or exit{PARTIAL,HUMAN}; at the final rung: heldout or exit{PARTIAL,OPEN}). A required failure with s ≥ 3 → the next record must be exit{PARTIAL, STALL}. Otherwise rounds continue. (8) ESCALATION: rung{name} requires probe{rung:name} before the next round, and s resets. rung E3 requires an earlier amend. (9) STOP: an open substrate with required:true requires exit{PARTIAL, OPEN} before any held-out. Held-out attempt 1 runs on best. Attempt 2 is allowed only on a version other than attempt 1's, with an all-required-pass Check at the final rung. A failed attempt 2 requires exit{PARTIAL, OVERFIT}. At most 2 attempts. (10) BUDGET: n ≤ budget.rounds. Round n+1 may start only if budget.minutes − elapsed ≥ 2 × the longest (t1 − t0) so far. The same rule applies to tokens if budget.tokens is set and every round reports tokens; otherwise it is unauditable. exit BUDGET requires a standing Check on the current best at the current rung. (11) STATUS: COMPLETE requires rung = final_rung, a Check on best at the final rung with all required pass and no required criterion unchecked, a held-out pass on best, and no required open substrate. exit COMPLETE otherwise is FALSE_COMPLETE; exit PARTIAL when all of these hold is MISLABEL (RECORD class). (12) OSCILLATION (advisory, AMBIGUOUS): compare each kept section's whitespace-normalized new text with any earlier best's text for that section (difflib ratio). A ratio ≥ 0.9 without exit OSCILLATION gives OSCILLATION_MISSED; exit OSCILLATION with a maximum ratio < 0.5 gives OSCILLATION_UNSUPPORTED. The prose '(nearly)' stays a human-visible judgment. (13) DRIFT: DONE after amends ≠ setup.done gives UNRECORDED_AMEND; a kept diff touching setup.check_files gives CHECK_FILE_EDIT; hashes ≠ setup.check_hashes gives CHECK_FILE_DRIFT. (14) CLASSES: VIOLATION = a keep, drop, Check value, halt, exit or held-out decision differs from the recomputed one. RECORD = an inconsistency that changes no decision. AMBIGUOUS = a declared policy parameter. Rules whose inputs are missing are unauditable.

controller.degraded_mode: There is no mode switch: prose is the only mode, and the loop runs identically without Python. The in-loop sentence ('If rqgm_check.py runs here, audit MEMORY each round; a violation pauses for the human') is inert when the file or Python is absent. Output then says the run was not audited, and the human may later run 'audit' on the saved or printed archive. A violation never rolls anything back; it pauses for the human, who decides. Missing fields make rules unauditable, not violated. Prose runs claim no atomic saves, no hard budget and no crash-safe resume; this is stated in the DESIGN/README non-guarantees. In the pilot, the P arm's workspace omits rqgm_check.py, so the shipped text runs byte-identical and prose-only.

substrate_interface: Defer: no adapter or envelope code, and no SKILL words. This is the judges' shared must_not, and no consumer exists. The peer's Scientific Loop substrate is design-only, with an in-memory reference kernel whose tests say nothing about RQGM. Mapping for later: the six slots already form the Substrate→RQGM half. request_id → the setup record. Target ref/hash → TARGET, hashed only by 'rqgm_check.py hash'. Parent snapshot → v0. Objective/rubric version → DONE plus the rung, with amend records. Evidence refs → GROUNDING. Budget allocation → BUDGET (rounds and time; tokens only if reported). The parent owns the allocation, and RQGM reports usage once. Stop conditions → the halts. Allowed capabilities stay with the host's permissions. The RQGM→substrate half will be computed, never self-reported: a future 'rqgm_check.py export MEMORY' emits the final version id and diff chain from v0, per-criterion status with how each was decided (command/source/judges/held-out/waived), amends, open gaps with owners, the first held-out result, rounds, time and tokens-or-null, judge model families, and the recomputed status, which takes precedence over any logged status. Receipt: a local COMPLETE is only a proposal, and the outer authority re-verifies it against its current snapshot and may reject it as stale; a stale receipt means a new run from the committed revision. Meta-Evaluator use: freeze the evaluator for the run, keep successor-development evidence apart from untouched evaluation evidence, and leave promotion to the outer authority. Commitment now: the records carry every field that export needs, and no prose rule depends on a substrate.

The orchestrator runs commands on a fresh copy with the check files as they were at setup; a check that edits files is ERROR. Failing a command best passes rejects the variant before judging; a failure best shares does not (C17). Hazard: literature (SpecBench 2605.21384); remedy design-only.

Row 2 (independence): add 2506.07962 (correlated errors, highest within a provider). Delete the Stance line that put held-out judges on the generator's model. Chat-only hosts: the human relays judges in fresh chats, else HALT(OPEN); the writer never judges.

Row 3 (signal): judge-1 order disagreement is now UNKNOWN, not a tie. Remove the paraphrase control (it changes clarity criteria). Adopt the compact seeded-defect probe per rung: judge 1 identity and seeded pairs in both orders, plus one Check judge, 5 calls. The seed is written by the orchestrator, never the generator. A miss turns on strict mode (all 3 judges, no early drop, 3/3 for keeps and Check passes) and tells the human. FLAWS bears on the Check; 2609.17857 is an open-weight preprint.
Row 4 (Goodhart): '15 of 47 screen rejections' becomes '13 substantive + 2 apply errors (e5-A, e18-B), now classed ERROR'. Screen rejections now enter the ledger's block (twice by the screen).

Delete 'every kept version beat the previous best, so no separate regression counter is needed' (pairwise preference is not transitive). Regressions are caught by the command gate, the protected veto, and re-marking every criterion at each Check.

Row 8 (generalization): RQGM 2606.26294 uses no majority vote, so the majority pass rule is an uncited design choice. 2510.11822's minority veto is an open question for Stage-6 calibration data. Spares run only on a changed best that passes a Check. The first held-out result is always reported. Held-out prompts are stored outside TARGET, GROUNDING, MEMORY and the repo, and are spent per TARGET.

Row 9 (stopping): the stall counts merit outcomes only. Two all-ERROR rounds → HALT(ERROR), a new halt. The budget is rounds and time from records, with tokens null unless reported, never estimated. Start a round only if the remaining time covers twice the costliest round, else Check, then HALT(BUDGET). A Check or held-out result stands until best, the rung or DONE changes. DONE and the rubric change only by amend.

Row 10 (state): delete 'a stable order makes resume deterministic'. Use round-atomic resume with a resume record and log-before-write. Cite the original '5 wasted re-runs on the broken resume' (log.md at 3dd6700); the 'out of order' cause was added in c3eebb2 and is not relied on. Replace '~6.8 vs ~11 agents per round' with 'calls per round, not cost per verified outcome'. Caching the judge prefix is a cost note, not a rule.

New row 11 (enforcement): the prose is the contract. Every rule is local, fail-closed and recomputable from verbatim un-blinded verdicts. The optional read-only rqgm_check.py audits and never decides. Motivation: measured (text dry-run), 10 then 8 ambiguous branches in the v2 dry-runs. Remedy: design-only. Promotion to code is pre-registered (Stage 1 thresholds; any decision-changing VIOLATION or journal mismatch in the pilot).

New 'Non-guarantees': prose runs make no claim of atomic saves, a hard budget or crash-safe resume. Held-out secrecy is only as good as where the human stores the prompts. validation:
STAGE 0 (now, zero model calls).
(a) Word caps by str.split, already measured on the drafts: SKILL 996/1000; INITIATOR 1295/1300, with THE LOOP at 957. README must stay ≤1250 and DESIGN ≤2200, checked by meta_tool.py caps_report after their edits.
(b) Implement rqgm_check.py and pass selftest (P01-P23). The positive fixtures guard against a reject-everything checker.
(c) Coverage map: every binding keep and every prose decision rule maps to a checker rule or is marked 'unauditable'. Binding keeps: writer never judges; no fabricated substrates; DONE and rubric never edited to pass; the human escalates and closes [OPEN]; held-out final check; domain-agnostic.
(d) Harness unit tests with fake adapters: timeout, malformed JSON, a late superseded result, and a ceiling hit mid-round (the run must still emit its last best for scoring). Scan every role capsule for sealed paths.
(e) Scorer sanity, run by the human because the scorer is sealed: score the untouched v0, the sealed references and the decoys, and confirm the scorer separates them.

STAGE 1 (decision-scenario test; runs first; about 90 short calls plus 1 GPT upload; budgeted separately from the pilot).
Scenarios: 30 frozen synthetic archive states, each with new results. Classes covered:
- ERROR vs tie, and judge-1 order disagreement.
- Judge-3 trigger, including UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN and tie/tie on a shorter variant.
- Strict keep and strict Check; prune on two ties; the protected veto.
- Command regression vs shared failure; tie-break.
- All-ERROR rounds and HALT(ERROR); stall count and when a Check is due.
- Standing-Check reuse; held-out fail → spare gating or HALT(STALL).
- The budget start rule; amend and E3; required vs optional [OPEN]; torn-line resume; escalation probe and stall reset.
Answer key: 'audit --pending'. The human adjudicates it against the prose before any scoring; a disagreement fixes the text or the code, followed by a re-freeze.
Runs: 3 fresh Claude contexts per scenario answer from SKILL.md alone. One GPT upload answers all 30 from the INITIATOR paste.
Report: exact-match misapplication per rule class.
Pre-registered: 3/30 or more errors in any context, or a class wrong in 2 or more of the 3 Claude contexts, makes that rule checker-mandatory where a shell exists (v3.1) and schedules a live enforcing arm. At most 1/30 in every context means 'prose carries it' survives Stage 1 only.

STAGE 2 (prep smoke, ≤20 calls, on a disposable toy target, not T1 or T2).
Harness: subagents cannot spawn subagents, so the Workflow script re-invokes the orchestrator per step with the arm's spec text, MEMORY and the returned role outputs. The orchestrator emits records and role requests. The script runs each role as a fresh subagent, decides nothing, journals raw I/O with SHA-256, and meters calls, tokens (as reported, else null) and time.
Cap: measure the minimal complete V and P paths (setup, probe, 2 rounds, Check, held-out) and set the per-run cap C = 1.25 × the larger path. Never use the peer's 30-call/60K-token cap: the only measured datum is about 60K subagent tokens per agent call.
The human approves total spend.
Freeze manifest.json before any scored call. It records:
- SHA-256 of V (24663bd), P (v3 bytes), rqgm_check.py, the fixtures, the scorer, the held-out prompts, the harness, and the S/B and role prompts; the model id; and C.
- The shared DONE. T1: t1-public command; t1-spec and t1-interface source; t1-clarity judges. T2: t2-numbers, t2-required, t2-claims and t2-unknowns source; t2-clarity judges; Q3 optional.
- The scripted human-proxy decisions: escalate when offered, never amend, never close an [OPEN], pick the newer version at OSCILLATION, approve no restructure.
- That the P workspace has no rqgm_check.py.

STAGE 3 (main runs). Tasks T1 and T2, plus T3 if the human writes it after the freeze (design-blind). Arms:
- S: one strong agent with the same tools, public tests, corpus and cap.
- B: fixed verification. Best-of-N fresh single revisions of v0, each gated by the same harness-run commands and one Verifier call. Select by public-check passes, then fewest Verifier flags, then length. No judges.
- V: frozen v2.
- P: v3 prose.
Protocol: one run per arm and task, randomized order, memory reset, and all roles in one model family (disclosed). The harness runs the sealed held-out prompts as the human proxy and passes only criterion IDs to the loop. S and B also run at 0.5×C for a two-point cost curve.
Endpoint: the sealed deterministic scorer on each final artifact.

STAGE 4 (fault runs; T1; V and P; cap C each). Inject the same faults at the same call indices in both arms:
- f1: an unparsable verdict at round-1 judge 2.
- f2: a duplicated diff anchor in round 1.
- f3: a check command that exceeds its timeout.
- f4: a real orchestrator kill and restart mid-round 2, reported separately from the simulated torn-tail fixture P18.
These runs are not compared with S or B.

STAGE 5 (audit and honesty, zero calls).
- Run 'audit --first' on every P archive. For V archives, report coverage only; they are mostly unauditable.
- compare.py checks each logged verdict against the journal's raw output, then the kept-text hash against the judged-input hash. It then recomputes the first decision divergence from the journal outputs, classes it VIOLATION or AMBIGUOUS under the frozen mapping, and never splices later outputs. Ambiguities found later become numbered manifest amendments before any result is read.
- Contamination scan: a call input containing a sealed filename or any 8-gram of the answer key voids that run.
- The human runs the sealed scorer.

STAGE 6 (judge calibration after all arms; about 48-72 calls). Per task, judge 4 human-seeded defects on the sealed reference plus 1 identity pair, using the arms' exact pairwise prompts (both orders) and Check prompts. Measure the pairwise miss rate, the Check false-pass rate and the order-reversal rate, and compare them with the in-run probe outcomes.

CROSS-FAMILY (≤3 GPT uploads):
(1) The Stage-1 scenarios.
(2) Blinded final artifacts per task, with per-criterion pass/fail on t1-clarity and t2-clarity plus an error hunt, compared with the scorer.
(3) An adversarial claim audit of the pilot report.

BUDGET. About 90 short calls in Stage 1, 20 prep, 10C main (8 full-cap runs plus 4 half-cap runs), 2C faults and about 72 calibration: roughly 700 calls at C = 45, plus 5C with T3. The human approves before Stage 3.
Hard 200-call fallback: Stage 1 at one context per scenario (30 calls), prep 18, and T2 × {P, V, S} × C with C ≤ 45. B, T1 and the fault runs then become the first follow-up. If C > 45, drop S before V.

PRE-REGISTERED.
Primary outcome: false completion (COMPLETE while the scorer finds a required failure), then oracle pass of the required criteria.
Secondary: decision-changing violations and journal mismatches per run; seeded-defect catch rate (probe and Stage 6); calls, tokens-or-null and minutes; human-proxy interventions; the exit distribution.
Predictions:
- V cannot COMPLETE T2 honestly, because v2 has no optional-[OPEN] path. This is true by construction: T2's optional field was co-designed with P's rule. It is disclosed and does not count as evidence.
- Under f1, V treats the ERROR as a tie or a rejection, or re-samples it, while P retries once and drops the variant.
- At least one probe miss occurs on the Check.
Decision rules:
- Any P false completion, decision-changing VIOLATION or journal mismatch makes that rule checker-mandatory where a shell exists, and withdraws the 'prose carries it' claim for that rule.
- P below S or B on the primary outcome for any task means no 'improved' claim.
- S or B at or above P on every task means reporting 'no advantage observed over simpler methods on these cases'.
- A Stage-6 false-pass rate above 50% means Check passes for that task type are reported as unreliable, and a minority-veto Check becomes the next candidate, tested prospectively.
Report results per case, with no significance claims.

WHAT IT CAN CONCLUDE.
- Whether the v3 prose executes end to end in this host within C.
- Per-case oracle outcomes, false completions and costs of P against S, B and V at matched caps.
- How often an LLM orchestrator misapplies each rule class, on synthetic states (Stage 1) and in live runs (audit plus journal).
- How f1-f4 were handled.
- Judge leniency on seeded defects, for these artifacts and one model family.

WHAT IT CANNOT CONCLUDE.
- General or statistically reliable superiority: n = 1 per cell, 2-3 small tasks, and possible ceiling effects.
- The effect of any single rule: V to P is a package.
- Cross-family independence: in-loop roles use one family, and the GPT uploads are spot checks.
- Usability for a real human in a plain chat, or behaviour of a continuous single-session orchestrator: the harness re-invokes the orchestrator per step.
- Behaviour at E3.
- Crash safety beyond f4.
- That the checker's rules are right: conformance is not correctness.
- Anything about enforcement: no enforcing arm runs.

risks: The prose-first bet may be false: LLM orchestrators may misapply the keep, stall and budget branches. Stage 1 and the pilot audit are the falsification tests, and promotion to code is pre-registered.

The audit checks internal consistency, not honesty: the orchestrator writes MEMORY. Records honesty is measured only by the pilot's comparison against the journal, and it stays unaudited in user runs.

Headroom is 4 words in SKILL and 5 in INITIATOR, so every pilot fix must displace text. About 20 cut tokens are formatting, the INITIATOR fence removes 60 '>' tokens, and each schema record counts as one str.split token. All of this is disclosed.
The compact probe tests only judge 1 and one Check judge, so lenient judges 2 and 3 go undetected until Stage 6. Seeds written by the orchestrator may be too easy.
Judges do not see command results, so a variant that only turns a failing command green still needs 2 judge preferences. T1 may stall; this is in the Deferred table with a trigger.

UNKNOWN on a protected criterion blocks pruning but does not veto an improvement keep; only an explicit 'best' does. This trades order-noise vetoes for some regression risk, and strict mode is the remedy.
The new HALT(ERROR) may end runs on flaky infrastructure after two all-ERROR rounds, and the judge-3 trigger may spend one extra call when two judges tie a non-shorter variant.
In plain-chat mode the Verifier and Screen still run in the writer's context. The relay is slow, and printed records can be torn or misordered. None of this has been tested with a real human.
Fail-closed defaults will raise PARTIAL and HALT rates, which may read as a regression unless Output and README explain them.
'(nearly)' remains a judgment, and the checker's 0.9 ratio is arbitrary and advisory.
The majority pass at the Check and held-out stays despite leniency literature. The probe detects leniency but only strict mode corrects it, and the held-out gate stays majority.
Two rule definitions exist (the prose and rqgm_check.py) and can drift. Fixtures prove conformance only, and any meta-run rule change invalidates the Stage-1 answer key until it is re-adjudicated.
'optional' could be used to escape a failing gap. It is set at Setup, a later change is an amend, and Output labels it, but none of this is enforced in prose.
The budget start rule ('twice the costliest round') is a heuristic, and the first round is unconstrained.
Deleting the Stance section (strongest model, 'deletions welcome', one agent at a time) may change user-run behaviour without evidence either way.

Pilot validity: one model family; per-step orchestrator re-invocation differs from a real session; n = 1 per cell; T2 favours P by construction; sealed files have no technical boundary; about 700 calls at an unmeasured per-call cost need human approval; B's N and selection rule could bias the comparison (frozen in the manifest).
v3, like v2, was designed outside any run. Every claim is design-only until the pilot logs a run.

Its 997-word draft is the starting text, and every graft is paid for with cuts; no cap is raised. Result: SKILL 996/1000 and INITIATOR 1295/1300, measured by str.split on scratchpad/synth-v3.

Controller: read-only, optional auditor only. All three judges' must_not exclude an owning controller. I merged evaluation-first's 'auditor, promoted on evidence' with prose-first's 'optional, read-only, ships beside SKILL', and kept controller-first's misapplication threshold as the Stage-1 promotion rule.
No sidecar rule files (all judges' must_not): the procedure and record schema stay in SKILL.md and inside the INITIATOR paste. PROSE_MODE.md and schema.md are rejected.

Command wiring (judge 1's fatal flaw in prose-first; controller-first PROSE_MODE step 2): failing a command *best* passes rejects the variant before judging, and a failure *best* shares does not (peer C17), so T1 can be repaired one change at a time. '`command` (you run it; it decides)' restores v2's override.

Pruning needs all 3 judges completed (all judges; controller-first C18/C19). The judge-3 trigger becomes 'unless judges 1 and 2 prefer the same version' (judge 3's UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN ambiguity), so ties and UNKNOWN never skip judge 3. Cost: possibly one unneeded call when two judges tie a non-shorter variant. Accepted for a one-branch rule and 11 saved words.
Strict mode also tightens the Check to 3/3 on judges criteria (judge 1: otherwise a probe that detects Check leniency changes nothing).
